label: rem:calibration-inputs
title: Calibration inputs and predictive content
html:
The QOU framework requires exactly three calibration inputs from experiment: the leptonic mass scale m_e (CAL-1), the neutron \beta-sector bar-skew channel P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} (CAL-2), and the pion-sector bar-even channel P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi} (CAL-3). Their numerical proxies are m_e, the ratio m_\mu/m_e (which pins q_0), and m_\pi. These inputs match the three real degrees of freedom of the first cohomology H^1(\mathrm{Bring}) = 2W. All other masses, binding energies, Q-values, and coupling constants are predictions. \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} serves as the CAL-2 proxy, validating the framework-derived hadronic energy scale \mathfrak{E}_0.

The three inputs

Input (proxy) CAL Canonical observable What it fixes Rel. precision
m_e = 0.51099895000 \pm 0.00000000015 MeV CAL-1 m_e (leptonic mass scale) the MeV unit + cohomological period 2.9 \times 10^{-10}
m_\mu / m_e = 206.7682830 \pm 0.0000045 CAL-2 P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} (n \beta-sector bar-skew channel) substrate q_0 (W-plane modulus) 2.2 \times 10^{-8}
m_\pi = 139.57039 \pm 0.00018 MeV CAL-3 P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi} (pion-sector bar-even channel) orthogonal meson scale (\mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{Hopf})=0) 1.3 \times 10^{-6}

CAL-2 cross-check (not a separate input). The free-neutron \beta-decay Q-value \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(n) = \hbar/P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} = 0.78233341 \pm 0.00000061 MeV is the proxy for CAL-2. The hadronic energy scale \mathfrak{E}_0 is framework-derived from (m_e, q_0); \mathfrak{Q}_\beta reproduced from q_0 then validates it to 0.17\% (subject to the net-ansatz caveat below). It is a cross-check, not a fourth calibration.

The first input is a dimensionless ratio — it fixes q_0 via the leading-order substrate-truncation of the canonical operator-valued mass formula (see the note on the superseded scalar density below):

\frac{m_\mu}{m_e} \;\stackrel{\text{LO}}{=}\; \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{\hbar_q^2}

(Skein mass relation), where \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.0299 is the topological constant (hyperbolic volume of the figure-eight knot) and \hbar_q = (q-1)/q. No units are involved. The precision is limited by the muon mass (2.2 \times 10^{-8}), not the electron (2.9 \times 10^{-10}).

Substrate density refinement. The dimensional factor 1/\hbar_q^2 forms the leading-order scalar substrate density. The canonical operator-valued form replaces it with the Wedderburn-graded expansion. The Skein form closes m_\mu/m_e = 206.77 because it evaluates the Kashaev q \to 1 limit (the hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)), dressed by the scalar 1/\hbar_q^2. The lepton-sector factor \xi_\ell(q) that replaces 1/\hbar_q^2 remains open.

The second input sets the leptonic mass scale — the conversion from dimensionless natural units to MeV. The electron is the natural choice: it is the simplest charged lepton, its mass is the most precisely measured particle mass in the Standard Model, and its brane tower is fully computable from q_0 alone:

  m_e(\text{natural})
  =
  \frac{\mathrm{Li}_2(q^{-2})}{\hbar_q^2}
  \approx  112

where \mathrm{Li}_2(q^{-2}) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} q^{-2n}/n^2 converges in \sim 20 terms. The conversion factor is then m_e(\text{MeV}) / m_e(\text{natural}) \approx 4.57 \times 10^{-3} MeV.

CAL-2 realization — the hadronic energy scale \mathfrak{E}_0 and the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta cross-check. (CAL-3 proper is the meson scale m_\pi; see below.) The leptonic inputs (m_e, q_0) give a framework-derived hadronic scale in two forms — the single-Planck-tick value \mathfrak{E}_0^{(N=0)} = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) \approx 4.186 MeV (energy scale) and the tower-summed \mathfrak{E}_0^{\text{full}} = \mathfrak{E}_0^{(N=0)}/(1-\hbar_q^2) \approx 4.228 MeV (beta-decay energy scale §"tower-summed form"). The free neutron \beta-decay Q-value calibrates \mathfrak{E}_0:

  \mathfrak{E}_0^{(\text{cal})}
  =
  \frac{\mathfrak{Q}_\beta(n)}{|\Delta(\mathrm{net})|}
  =
  \frac{0.78233}{|h(h-2)/2|}
  \approx  4.179 \text{ MeV}

(The typed-crossings 6-term decomposition yields \lvert\Delta(\text{net,typed})\rvert \approx 0.18829 and a slightly smaller \mathfrak{E}_0 \approx 4.155 MeV; the 0.6% gap is finite-size noise in the typed decomposition — see beta-decay-energy-scale §"three values".)

where \Delta(\mathrm{net}) = h(h-2)/2 is the symbolic NF difference between neutron and proton (symbolic Q-value). The free neutron is the simplest hadronic decay — one crossing change (\mathfrak{d} \to \mathfrak{u}) inside one nucleon, no nuclear environment. Once \mathfrak{E}_0 is fixed, \mathfrak{Q}_\beta cross-check gap. With the tower form \mathfrak{E}_0^{\text{full}} active, the framework-derived value overshoots the calibrated value by +1.75\%. The geometric series direction does not close the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residual; it widens it. This leaves an explicit residual requiring categorical-derivation review.

Fitting constraint. The relation \mathfrak{Q}_\beta = |\Delta(\mathrm{net})| \cdot \mathfrak{E}_0 constitutes an ansatz. The unweighted \mathrm{net} sum differs structurally from the Markov-trace weighted sums of the mass tower. Until resolved by direct per-braid computation, the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta-from-q_0 reproduction remains an unclosed cross-check.

Necessity of exactly three inputs

The Lagrangian endomorphism \Phi \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A) (categorical action) lives in a vector space of dimension \dim \mathrm{End}(A) = (\dim A)^2. For H_3(R, q) this is 6^2 = 36 in principle. The on-shell constraint \star_q F_\nabla = F_\nabla (instanton on-shell) and gauge invariance \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 (observability) eliminate all but three real parameters:

  1. The deformation parameter q. This is the single continuous parameter of the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(R, q). It controls all dimensionless ratios: mass ratios, coupling constants, crossing asymmetries. The observability condition forces q \neq 1 (otherwise \mathrm{Ad}(A) has invariants), and the Descartes condition \chi(A) = -6 constrains q to a one-parameter family, but does not fix a specific value. The value q_0 \approx 1.110 is fixed by one dimensionless measurement.

  2. The leptonic mass scale. The categorical mass \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)) (categorical mass as Markov trace) is dimensionless (signed at the categorical level; the archimedean specialization at q_0 takes the positive observable value by Wenzl positivity for canonical T_w). Converting to physical units (MeV) requires one mass measurement. The electron mass sets this scale, analogous to the speed of light c and Planck's constant \hbar in the Standard Model.

  3. The orthogonal meson scale (CAL-3 = P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi}, proxy m_\pi). The brane tower converts the single-level Hecke algebra to full particle masses, but the meson sector carries an orthogonal class (\mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{Hopf})=0) genuinely independent of (m_e, q_0) — the charged-pion mass m_\pi fixes it (SDP-validated). The hadronic \beta-decay scale \mathfrak{E}_0 is derived from (m_e, q_0) and cross-checked by \mathfrak{Q}_\beta (the CAL-2 proxy), so it is not the third independent input. The three inputs correspond to the three physical sectors: shape (q, via P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}/CAL-2), leptonic size (m_e/CAL-1), meson scale (m_\pi/CAL-3).

No further parameters exist because:

  • The knot-particle dictionary is determined by \chi = -6: exactly 6 embeddable torus knots, no choice (cohomological embedding).
  • The crossing weights q and -q^{-1} are eigenvalues of the R-matrix, determined by q alone.
  • The typed crossing operators C(f_i, f_j; \sigma_k) are determined by the Hecke relation and quark flavors, no free parameters (typed crossing operator).
  • The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M is unique (up to the Markov parameter z, which is determined by q) by Schur orthogonality (RJ canonical inner product).

Predictions from the three inputs

From q_0 alone (dimensionless):

  • Lepton mass ratios: m_\tau/m_e, m_\tau/m_\mu
  • Hecke amplitude: h = q - q^{-1} \approx 0.209
  • Crossing asymmetry: q/q^{-1} \approx 1.231 (matter/antimatter)
  • Neutron-proton splitting structure: m_n - m_p \propto \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}} - \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}}
  • Pair production polarisation selection rule
  • All NF decompositions and operator selection weights

From q_0 + m_e (in MeV):

  • Muon mass: m_\mu = m_e \times \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 (first prediction, by construction matches calibration input)
  • Proton mass: via Skein pair formula + dressed quark masses from Skein resolution tree (tractable computation)
  • Neutron mass: m_n = m_p + \mathfrak{Q}_\beta (Hecke engine)
  • Deuteron binding energy: \Delta E_D \approx 2.224 MeV
  • Beta decay Q-values: 6 benchmarks at 4.4% MAE
  • Nuclear shell structure and magic numbers
  • Half-life predictions

Structurally predicted (verified against CODATA):

  • Neutron-proton splitting: m_n - m_p from crossing pair isolation (categorical, no calibration beyond q_0)
  • Q-value ratios: dimensionless, from q_0 alone
  • Shell structure and magic numbers: from transfer matrix eigenvalues at q_0

Open (concrete computation, not conceptual gap):

  • Dressed quark mass \mu_\mathfrak{u} from q_0 alone: requires Skein resolution of Borromean braid (\leq 729 terms, each requiring a hyperbolic volume computation)
  • Binding energy per nucleon B/A: same Skein resolution approach

Comparison with the Standard Model

The Standard Model has 19 free parameters (6 quark masses, 3 lepton masses, 3 CKM angles + 1 phase, 3 gauge couplings, Higgs mass, Higgs VEV, QCD theta angle). The QOU framework replaces all 19 with 3 (one dimensionless ratio + two mass/energy scales), deriving the rest from the topology of the Bring surface \Sigma_4 and the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(R, q).

The reduction from 19 to 3 is possible because:

  • Particle content is topological (from \chi = -6), not a free choice
  • Mass ratios are knot invariants (from Vol and \mathrm{tr}_M), not free parameters
  • Coupling constants are R-matrix eigenvalues (from q), not independent inputs
  • Mixing angles are Clebsch--Gordan coefficients of the knot eigenbasis decomposition

⚠ Vintage: this row is CODATA 2018, not 2022 (measured 2026-09-05, qou-i229). 206.7682830 \pm 0.0000045 is the CODATA-2018 muon–electron mass ratio; CODATA 2022 gives 206.7682827 \pm 0.0000046, and the substrate reads the latter from the NIST table (qou_substrate.constants.MASS_RATIO_MU_E) since 2026-08-15. epistemic-status-of-calibrations already records that this literal is 2018.

The value is not changed here: it is CAL-2 itself, so substituting it moves q_0 and every quantity derived from it, which is the tracked refresh in qou-i229 and not a labelling fix. The discrepancy is 1.451 ppb (0.065\sigma) — physically nothing, which is why it survived the 2026-08-15 drain that fixed the same literal across computations/.
